script: In Japan dating can feel less like romance and more like a job interview. You sit across from someone for a few minutes. Name age job hobbies. Then the timer ends and the next person sits down. These events are called konkatsu parties. Marriage hunting. And the goal is not to casually flirt for months. It is to find someone serious enough to build a future with. Some people check salary. Some check family plans. Some check if you want kids where you want to live and how stable your job is. To foreigners this can look brutally unromantic. But in Japan where work is exhausting and time is limited some people want to skip the games. No endless situationship. No guessing for half a year. Just one question hiding behind every smile. Could I marry this person or not?
title: The Great Emu War
hook_text: In Japan dating can feel less like romance and more like a job interview.
